descriptions.draft: Build, run and document Boolean literature searches for Scopus (users may say "Opus"), Web of Science (WoS) and Google Scholar. Use it whenever someone gives a research title, topic, question or systematic, scoping or bibliometric review and wants search strings, keywords or a concept table; wants the strings run and the hit counts recorded; wants the free or full-text papers a search finds downloaded into a folder; or wants a search strategy report or PRISMA flow diagram for their database search. Also use it to debug, fix, shorten, widen or narrow a search they already wrote, including an "invalid query", zero results, or too many or too few hits. Handles field tags (TS=, TITLE-ABS-KEY, PY=), AND/OR/NOT, truncation (*), wildcards (?), phrase quotes, country niches, several year ranges, broad to narrow tiers, and Malay or other local-language strings. Not for screening abstracts, writing the review itself, a literature review matrix, or general Boolean or SQL help.
descriptions.optimized: Use this skill for academic database searching on Scopus (also called "Opus"), Web of Science (WoS) and Google Scholar. Turn a research title, topic or review type (systematic, scoping, bibliometric) into Boolean search strings, keywords or a concept table. Run the strings and record hit counts, download the free full-text papers found, or produce a search strategy report or PRISMA flow diagram. Also use it whenever someone pastes a search string they already wrote and asks about it: is it too long, too broad or narrow, returning zero results, an "invalid query", or needs shortening, fixing or adapting to another database. Covers field tags (TS=, TITLE-ABS-KEY), AND/OR/NOT, truncation, wildcards, phrase quotes, country niches, year ranges, and Malay or other local-language strings. Not for screening abstracts, writing the review, literature matrices, picking manuscript keywords, or general Boolean, regex or SQL help.
